about.title: Del Mar Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Del Mar is a small town — about 4,351 residents along a short stretch of coast — and when someone here dies because of another person's carelessness, the loss ripples through the whole community. In 2025, public records show 17 injury collisions and 22 people hurt on Del Mar streets, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. Fatal crashes are uncommon here, yet families still lose loved ones on Camino Del Mar or Del Mar Heights Road, in a hospital bed, or at a workplace across the county. California's wrongful death statute gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a claim, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. Recoverable losses cover funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive connects Del Mar families with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency, at no cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Del Mar Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out your family's standing before anything else moves forward.

items.title: The two-year clock, watched closely
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is far shorter when a government entity may be responsible. Connecting early keeps those deadlines from slipping.

items.title: Every category of loss accounted for
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance are all recognized under California law. Network attorneys work on contingency, so pursuing them costs nothing upfront.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on Via De La Valle or Carmel Valley Road. Where do we begin?
items.answer: Start by requesting the collision report from the responding agency and keeping any hospital, funeral and insurance paperwork together. Both roads carry heavy volumes through the Del Mar area, so there may be witnesses, nearby cameras or other records worth preserving quickly. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who will review the facts and explain your options without any fee.

items.question: Del Mar recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that affect whether we have a case?
items.answer: Not at all. Wrongful death claims arise from far more than local traffic — a crash elsewhere in San Diego County, a medical error, a workplace incident, or neglect in a care facility can all support a claim. The public-record count for one small town has no bearing on whether your family's loss was preventable.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, entirely separate from any criminal case, and it can proceed on its own track. Waiting can be risky because the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court. An attorney can explain how the two proceedings may interact in your situation.
